title: City of Pundranagara
description: A fortified city stands on the Karatoya river, and a Brahmi inscription found there is the oldest known writing from Bengal.

title: Somapura Mahavihara built
description: The Pala king Dharmapala builds one of the largest Buddhist monasteries of the subcontinent, a centre of learning for four centuries.

title: Bakhtiyar Khalji conquers Bengal
description: A cavalry raid by Bakhtiyar Khalji drives out the Sena king Lakshmana Sena and begins more than five centuries of Muslim rule in Bengal.

title: Conquest of Sylhet
description: An army of the sultan of Lakhnauti, joined by the Sufi Shah Jalal, takes Sylhet, and Islam spreads in north-eastern Bengal.

title: Bengal Sultanate unified
description: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah takes Sonargaon and unites Bengal in one independent sultanate that lasts two centuries.

title: Sixty Dome Mosque
description: Khan Jahan Ali completes the largest mosque of the sultanate in the city he founded at the edge of the Sundarbans.

title: Battle of Rajmahal
description: A Mughal army defeats and kills Daud Khan Karrani, the last sultan, and Bengal becomes a Mughal province.

title: Dhaka made capital of Bengal
description: The governor Islam Khan moves the capital of Mughal Bengal to Dhaka, which grows into a major trading city known for its muslin.

title: Mughal conquest of Chittagong
description: Shaista Khan's forces take the port from the kingdom of Arakan and end Arakanese and Portuguese slave raiding in Bengal.

title: Pabna peasant uprising
description: Tenant farmers form a league and refuse rent increases demanded by landlords, leading to the Bengal Tenancy Act of 1885.

title: University of Dhaka opens
description: The first university in eastern Bengal begins teaching and becomes the centre of the region's political life.

title: Noakhali riots
description: Attacks on Hindus in the Noakhali district kill thousands in the year before Partition, and Gandhi walks through the villages to restore peace.

title: Sylhet referendum
description: Voters in the Sylhet district of Assam choose to join East Bengal in Pakistan.

title: Language Movement shootings
description: Police fire on students demanding that Bengali be a state language of Pakistan, a day now marked as International Mother Language Day.

title: United Front election victory
description: A coalition of Bengali parties defeats the ruling Muslim League in the East Bengal provincial election.

title: Six-point programme
description: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman sets out six demands for the autonomy of East Pakistan, which become the programme of the Awami League.

title: Bhola cyclone
description: The deadliest tropical cyclone on record kills at least 300,000 people, and anger at the government's response strengthens the autonomy movement.

title: Sheikh Mujib's 7 March speech
description: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman tells a crowd of about a million to prepare for a struggle for independence.

title: Operation Searchlight
description: The Pakistan Army attacks students, police and political activists in Dhaka, beginning the Bangladesh Liberation War and the killing of civilians that accompanies it.

title: Declaration of independence
description: Bangladesh is declared independent in the name of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman as the army crackdown begins, a day kept as Independence Day.

title: Mujibnagar government sworn in
description: The provisional government of Bangladesh takes its oath in a mango grove near the Indian border and directs the war from exile.

title: Killing of intellectuals
description: Two days before the surrender, the Pakistan Army and local collaborators abduct and kill teachers, doctors, writers and journalists.

title: Constitution takes effect
description: The first constitution establishes a parliamentary republic founded on nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism.

title: Assassination of Sheikh Mujib
description: Army officers kill the founding president and most of his family at his home, beginning fifteen years of coups and military rule.

title: Assassination of Ziaur Rahman
description: President Ziaur Rahman is killed by army officers in a failed coup.

title: Ershad's coup
description: The army chief Hussain Muhammad Ershad overthrows the elected president and rules for nearly nine years.

title: Ershad resigns
description: Weeks of mass protest force Ershad from office, and elections in 1991 restore parliamentary government.

title: Cyclone of 1991
description: A cyclone and storm surge strike the south-eastern coast and kill about 138,000 people.

title: Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord
description: The government and the hill peoples' party sign an agreement ending two decades of insurgency in the south-east.

title: State of emergency
description: After months of street violence over a disputed election the president declares an emergency and a caretaker government backed by the army rules for two years.

title: Rana Plaza collapse
description: An eight-storey building housing garment factories collapses and kills 1,134 people, the deadliest accident in the history of the clothing industry.

title: Rohingya exodus begins
description: A military campaign in Myanmar drives more than 700,000 Rohingya across the border, where they settle in the world's largest refugee camp.
